reviews.comment: Mr. Kebo was an amazing professor for a class that's typically difficult. If you go to lectures and pay attention, you'll be fine since he explains everything really well. Homework is fairly straightforward, but do it early because it's always pretty long. Tests are online and open-note and are fairly doable given the time alotted.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had him for 313, so I knew his style coming in. He does a lot of hands-on teaching with in-class activities and five labs using xv6 linux. At times, the lectures can get mundane. You will have one midterm and one final that are both take-home and open-notes. Overall a good course except for labs 3 and 4.

His approach to teaching OS is different from and a lot easier than other professors. However, I still feel like I understood what's going on during labs and the lecture explanations were good. Main complaint is the pop quizzes are less application and more copy/paste from slides, along with lectures occasionally being boring.

In my opinion, taking OS with Kebo is a waste of time if you actually want to learn anything. Every 2-3 weeks, he assigns a "lab" (homework) that involves adding new features to a toy OS (xv6). The problem is that he gives everyone sample code and step-by-step instructions, so you basically don't need to think. Also, lecture quizzes are annoying.

David Kebo is a good professor, he hosts office hours consistently and forces you to learn the material. My main gripe with him are the activities, which are weighted extremely heavily. You would think this is a good thing, but they are timed, pretty hard, and sometimes the same day as you learned the content. Otherwise, take him. Great prof.

Great lecture materials, but not the best lectures. If you read his slides and the materials he asks you to look at before lecture, you'll do fine.

Exams are a pain though. They're take-home, but they're so long they can reasonably take 8 hours. Think I learned a great deal from this class though.

I took this class previously, and I'm sad because idk systems/networks as well as I wish I did. HW guides were long and often half-baked. Collaboration was discouraged. I asked a TA for help in office hours, and he suggested using ChatGPT, which started my bad vibe coding habit. You'll get a good grade, but you won't learn much and feel unfulfilled

A pretty straightforward class, but some programming assignments were pretty difficult. Study the slides and attend classes to do activities; those will help the most on exams, which were pretty easy. Lectures were a little hard to sit through since he spends a lot of it typing demonstrations, but make an effort and you should be fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Grading are more lab and in-class activity focused, but is overall easy as long as you spend enough time in it. His exams are fair in difficulty, but what to study for it is somewhat unclear. His lectures jumps between stuff frequently, and you can learn something from it if you pay attention but overall not anything in depth.

Kebo takes a different perspective on learning. His 313 course is not test-heavy, but rather lab and participation-heavy. The labs were very interesting and doable. During lecture, he jumps between the slides and examples, although at times they were a bit difficult to follow. Overall, he is a great professor that I enjoyed learning from.

Kebo is a straightforward guy and shows you everything you need to know in class plus he published the coding examples from class on GitHub. He doesn't take attendance but does random in-class activities based on examples he showed earlier in class. Tests are easy if you study. Strongly recommend.

Kebo is the goat. Class is not hard if you do in class activities. Lectures are pretty interesting later in the semester and Labs are straightforward. Just don't be an idiot and be respectful and you will be fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super disorganized course, and it only seemed like he cared for a select few classes. Would add tests to the autograder after assignments were due, including for exams. Easy to do well in, but won't prepare you if you want to take any kind of low level programming courses in the future
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Random in class activities made this class annoying. Also, he is very much against answering questions during the activities. However, that class is still very easy so worth. Def take.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kebo is a good teacher and makes the content easy. There are pop "quizzes" (in-class activities) in which you sometimes get very little time to complete them. The only reason my rating is low is because he is pretty blunt, rude, and inconsiderate sometimes. He makes rude remarks when a students laptop doesn't work, even though they know the content
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Does a good job answering questions in lecture and clarifying. Lecture notes are posted online. Programming assignment heavy, exams were very easy.

Dr. Kebo is the right choice for this class -- stay away from Kumar! The grade is heavily weighed with programming assignments, so put in the work early and they're easy 100s. Midterm and final each only worth 10%, so not stressful. Usually a graded activity every couple of classes. Be prepared for those. Good lectures, nice guy. Also, don't cheat.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very fun professor and seems like a genuinely great guy. Always willing to answer questions in class to make sure you understand the concepts. I had three years of prior coding experience so this class wasn't too difficult for me, but I could see this class being a little too much for someone new to coding. Would overall recommend.
Professor Kebo is amazing! CSCE 313 is typically a hard course but felt like a breeze thanks to him. Would 100% recommend.

313 is a pretty difficult class to begin with, but taking it with Dr. Kebo makes it a lot easier. His lectures are great and explain everything you need to know to be successful. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, I would highly recommend going as his in-class examples are a great way to learn the concepts.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great lecturer that made me learn lots of applicable concepts towards computer science/engineering (Linux, Basics of OS, Multithreading, Sockets/Packets, Cryptography). 2 open note all-day exams and quizzes every other week, and for LEs and PAs start early! Labs are office hours, and you'll gain an intuitive understanding of content over time.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: King Kebo the goat. Attendance not mandatory but has in class assignments, so try not to skip. Exams not worth a lot so focus on PAs and LEs. Has 1 extension day to use on any PA. Content not the most difficult, hard to understand at first but intuitive after. Open note all-day exams. Labs not mandatory, basically office hours.

One critique: Consider extra credit. The class is for beginners, but you'll quickly notice extra credit is tailored towards intermediate to advanced Python users. Balanced extra credit, for ex., could be to add an extra output to a print result, or to make the output look different. Not to go from printing simple results to recursive functions.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I converted my religious beliefs to Davidism. This guy is a legend. Loved his course and was inspired by his lectures. I would recommend David to anyone looking to have a good experience in learning computer science. This man is a genius and I am glad I took his course. This professor changed my academic perspective for the better.

Kebo is a great professor and a talented lecturer. He makes class engaging and entertaining while teaching the material in an understandable way. 313 is not an easy class, but he provides extra credit opportunities, and it is very clear what you need to get an A in the class. Almost half of your grade is 5 programming assignments, start early!

Cares a lot about the success of his students. This class pulls in concepts from a wide range of areas of computer science, he understands all of them really well and does a great job teaching the class. The extra credit hour for the lab is for good reason; homeworks and lab exercises are time consuming and at times have vague instructions.

Everything in this class is pretty reasonable. I personally wasn't that interested in the material but Kebo was passionate about teaching it. Exams are open-note but take several hours. Programming assignments make up most of the grade. Overall not a bad prof for this class, you can easily get an A if you put in a bit of work.

I really enjoyed the lectures. They felt relevant and he would often use lecture time to explain the PAs and LEs. Assignments are difficult but TAs and prof help. He also would explain and answer questions about the exams which were take home and to be finished by midnight. Overall a lot of work, but he gives you everything you need to do well.

Took Kebo for 313. Overall pretty good experience, the lectures themselves can be a bit boring but nonetheless found it pretty easy. The Labs and PA's are actually pretty interesting though, even though they can be a bit difficult.

(CSCE 313) Stale lectures; amazing TAs; PA difficulties: 5 < 4 < 1 < 2 < 3; Take home exams. Kebo is a great prof for 222 and not a hard grader overall. You can argue for points, and gives partial credit for programming questions on exams, just make sure it compiles / you tried something. The discord helps A TON on PAs, If you're stuck, look it up.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took him for 313. I enjoyed the lectures, but the homework was hard and sometimes long. There are a lot of resources provided if you aren't understanding concepts. Take home/online tests and quizzes are a huge plus.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had him for 222 and now 221. He is good, not great and not terrible. I like Kebo as a prof and how he makes the tests online and open note, it makes it less stressful. However I hate the homeworks and the way the TAs and the auto graders work. He doesnt do too hard of quizzes/tests which is awesome.

CSCE 110 is a pretty easy class if you have previous coding knowledge but the way professor Kebo organizes the class was simply awful. The labs are long, unclear, and had confusing grading criteria, labs were graded late, and the professor never answered emails. If you have experience programming in Python this will be an easy class regardless.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: 1st time teaching this, EXTREMELY disorganized, you learn the material for the lab as you do it which make it confusing. always behind, never enough time to learn the new stuff, took 3 weeks on linked lists. ok lectures, 1 pt of extra credit from in class act, and 90 is A, not 89.5. and a long project at the end. Honestly avoid imo, TA saved my B

(for 465, actually. it was not option)
I heard Kebo was GOATed for 222, so I thought, of course I will take him for 465. Big mistake! Lectures were boring and most days, he just talk about how to set up the HW, not even what was in the HW. Hard to reach outside of class and very rude. Take with Carlisle or someone who is a better lecturer and nice.

The only thing on the syllabus is when Exams and Labs are due, everything else is announced a couple of days before. Grading is very difficult and takes forever for anything to be graded. Lectures are him talking about a couple of things that are not related to assignments at the time. TA's and not very good or helpful.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Much harder than expected for an intro. Labs come with very poor instruction but perfection is expected to receive full credit. Expect this course to take an extra 10-15 hrs. Prof is very rude, impatient, and receives criticism poorly. Every reading/quiz/&EXAM is announced week of, leaving very little time for planning. Syllabus is very "loose".

His 221 is not a bad class when it comes to the lecture, but the labs are on another level. They are difficult and can be hard to understand. Even so, Dr. Kebo may not be the best choice for 221 but he is a god when it comes to 222.

The class structure is alright, but when it comes to the labs, which are a huge portion of the grade (30%), it is unorganized, and many of the TA's and peer teachers grade extremely difficult. I've had labs that have passed all autograder test cases, and then receive 50s and 60s. Kebo isn't bad, but his TA's make it much harder.

The class isn't difficult at all, the professor just has a bad attitude. Care's more about saving himself time, not students learning. He takes any issue with course structure as a personal attack, the poor response to criticism is what makes me feel like he isn't fit to be a lecturer.

He is such a nice professor who is willing to connect with students. My only challenge was that the TA was a tough grader who took forever to grade. Do lots of practice problems from the textbook or redo homework for practice. He also really cares about attendance, so it's important to always go to class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I like Dr Kebo as a person & hes very passionate about what he does but what he teaches in lectures vs whats in the homework is so different. His TAs take off points for the stupidest things. youll spend most of your time formatting hw bc he makes you type it all out. Some people like his style while some dont. Open note tests are awesome tho!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Kebo's a nice and funny guy, however the class itself isn't the best. It feels like he took three classes and put them into one. He also grades strict. After the assembler project, it feels like the entire course just fell apart. The lectures usually have nothing to do with the assignments. You would be better off learning by doing the assignments.

I love Kebo. He's a great professor and it shows when I was in class. He is a bit of a tough grader, but he makes up for it by doing extra credit during classes and he's just a cool guy. Take him for 222 and I promise you will pass that class
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Definitely the heaviest workload Ive ever had from a single class. Just make sure you stay on top of the million assignments that keep on dropping weekly. Some people say that he is a good professor but in my opinion his lectures had absolutely nothing to do with the tests or the labs. Im just happy the nightmare is over.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Kebo is a solid Prof. I struggled in the class but it was mostly my own fault. There are lots of different types of assignments for this class and TAs grade incredibly harshly. Lectures were decent and the slides were really helpful. Quiz and practice activities every week and homework assigned every other week. 3 take home exams noncumulative.

Kebo is most definitely the best professor to take with regards to CSCE222; tests, quizzes, and the homeworks were all through Gradescope, and the course syllabus was formatted extremely well. However, the TAs for the class will grade harshly, so be aware of that. I had an A in the class although my HW average was low. Tests were easier than review

Dr. Kebo clearly cared about students' learning, however, there are some annoying things to keep in mind: all proofs and math equations are typed, so 90% of the time spent on long homework assignments is formatting the answers. Since everything is web based, you must stay attentive of minor details that you might not have to writing.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Homework can take quite a while to complete, and they don't always relate to the lectures very well. Grading is very tough sometimes, I have lost a lot of points for even the simplest mistakes. Exams and quizzes are take home and open note which is nice. Not a bad professor but not great either, just mediocre at best.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kebo was a great professor. He can sometimes be a bit ride but he doesn't mean any harm. For the most part, the lectures have been helpful although the book does provide some good examples. There was not any coding in this class and was very conceptual which I like. It's very relaxed and there is nothing difficult here. Enjoy the course!

Dr Kebo is an amazing professor. The lectures were always fun to attend, and he goes over a lot of examples in class. He explains things very well. Start the homeworks in advance though because they are time consuming.

Great lecturer, though talks a bit slow at times. He's fair about grading and makes it very clear what the expectations are for this class at the beginning. You do have to learn LaTeX for this class, which takes a bit of time to get used to. Class has a fair amount of work, and does not include any coding, though code examples are sometimes used
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best lecturers I've had. He explains things slowly and makes it easy to understand. Everything was open note including exams. Great guy all around. It's not a difficult class but it might be with a different professor
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kebo is such an amazing professor. He records his lectures and does a lot of example problems in class in order to help prepare us for exams. His exams and homework aren't difficult either.

Dr. Kebo is great, take him if you can! The tests are usually open note or limited notes. His grading criteria is well laid out and he gives tons of partial credit. He filters out the busy work and condenses the material to only the useful info. He isn't a push over and won't just give you points because you are sad.

Never coded before, but I love coding in Python now. The semester's fairly easy and his lectures are recorded, but the ZyBook teaches you more imo since it gives more detail and you apply what you learn. CSCE110 is definitely for people who like to think logically/intuitively. Assessments are open-note. Not a bad prof, but you mostly teach yourself

I got an A in this class and I had very little coding experience. I learned a ton in this class but I definitely had to work for it. The labs were probably the hardest part but the harder ones you get two weeks to complete. I got a 97 on the first exam because it was open book. The TA/Prof aren't much help, but the internet answers everything.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is not the professor for non-CSCE majors. His quizzes are worded poorly, his regrade request policy is all show, and he is honestly one of the least helpful professors I've ever met. You will learn python, and your code may be perfect, but deviate from what he wants even a little and you can kiss your grades goodbye.

I took this class for the summer and Dr. Kebo is really great! He explains concepts well and gives us lots of examples to look at. I'm new to Python but he's great at helping his students understand. He's also a really nice guy.

Great teacher for beginner programming. I took him (during the pandemic) online and he hosted live lecture through zoom. He posted the recordings of the live lectures on youtube the same day. He really takes his time to explain everything and moved at a somewhat slow pace. But this pace was perfect for me as a beginner. Assignments were reasonable!

Dr. Kebo is a fantastic professor. However, I feel that his exams were unfair--written with little partial credit. I didn't do well on the exams (mostly C's and low B's), but if you do well on the labs you can get the A. He has pop quizzes and activities (easy). I felt I was unprepared for the project (but COVID was happening, so that could be why)
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Kebo is probably the best choice for 312; that being said, it's a tough class. You will have to work if you want to do well. Kebo's labs are much easier than the other professor's labs. My only gripe is that sometimes the material is unclear, and once on a test I've gotten a question wrong for answering explicitly what the book says.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kebo is approachable. Go to office hours! It's difficult to "code on the fly" during exams, so practice ahead of time! The questions are challenging but doable with practice. Take advantage of numerous resources like the supplemental book, Mosh's YouTube Python tutorials, & more. Work ahead, don't do labs on the due date, & ask questions!

Three exams @ 15%, 8 labs @ 25%, etc. Bit misleading. Exams outweigh everything. Don't fall for, "Pass the labs & you'll be fine." Those w/ high scores will be experienced in Python, just ask around. Beginners will struggle for Bs and Cs. This is an intro course & should be graded as such. Test for concepts on exams, not full blown lab questions.

Class suffers from a paradox. Extra credit in labs & exams given to improve grades, but those who benefit most are experienced in Python with 100s. Novices will spend most of their time piecing together the problems and debugging. No time to attempt the extra credit. Hopefully a system can be in place that helps both novices & gurus improve.

Kebo is a great professor who challenges his students. Indeed, the quizzes and exams are difficult and hard to finish in time. The labs, omg, were so hard I pulled my hair out, because the knowledge needed to complete them came after they were due, but Kebo still gave enough time for them. The index note cards to help on exams were nice too.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is definitely your best option for 222. Exams aren't too hard to get Bs or As on and the homework brings up your grade. There are quizzes but just make sure you know how to do the homework before the quizzes and you should be fine. Group assignments in class are also helpful as check-ins to make sure you are actually paying attention.

Dr Kebos class is a lot of work. There are always tons of assignments. He is a decent prof bht his lectures get a little boring sometimes. I thought it was a really hard class and I went in there knowing basic python already. there is extra credit though so thats good. 3 tests, 8 labs, 8 quizzes, in class activities, a group project, and homework
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kebo is a solid prof. He obviously understands the material he's teaching and wants his students to know it too. He is very conscious of questions and slows down if the class agrees he is going too fast. The material itself is very abstract and can be difficult, but Kebo tries his best and makes himself accessible. A very decent choice.

Dr. Kebo is one of the profs that makes me feel like my tuition costs are worth it. This class isn't easy, but getting a good grade is manageable and you will learn useful skills along the way. He explains things slowly and clearly, and provides lots of resources to succeed. Tests are the hardest part, but hw and the final project aren't that bad.

Class has 3 tests (some coding by hand on paper). Allowed to use a 3x5 notecard on tests but still dont underestimate the difficulty. There is 1 lab/week. Each lab has you code various tasks. Difficulty peaks around lab 4. Quizzes in class over recent lectures. Class isn't very difficult, it just takes practice. Dr. Kebo is a fantastic teacher.

Finally, a computer science professor you'll actually like. When assigning labs, he provides examples for how the code should look like, so it's not a "hit or miss". He assigns plenty of time for each lab (about 1-2 weeks). CSCE 110 with Kebo (Dr. Houngninou) are a great starting point for a student wanting to get started in computer programming.

Dr. Kebo puts so much into making his students successful. He offered a lot of extra credit opportunities that were simple in class group activities. The homework is from the book and it helps to do the homework before each quiz even if it isn't due until after the quiz. The test were straight forward, but make sure to watch the clock. My fav prof!

From what I've heard, he's one of the best choices for CSCE 222. The grade is made up of hw from the textbook, quizzes, and tests. You get a one page cheat sheet for the tests (final included) and the final isn't cumulative. The tests are pretty long. You do activities in class with your tablemates that will be extra credit, so go to class.
Just be thankful if you get him for this class.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ok, first of all some of these reviews below i feel like they are a bit inaccurate. They aren't wrong. Kebo is good but he's not great. He wont tell you everything you need to know on the tests. His teaching can be clear at times but confusing for some. I feel like if people think he's the best its a bit of an overstatement. He is just ok.

First semester he's teaching here but from what I heard from people in other classes, he seems to be the best professor for this CSCE 222. Just do the homework and show up for quizzes and tests and it'll be an easy A.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Kebo is a great professor for CSCE222. He makes sure students understand the material, so he shows a lot of examples. There are 7 HWs, 5 quizzes,and Extra Credit activities which are taken with your table partners. If you do all your homework, attend classes, it shouldn't be a problem to get an A or a B. He allows to use a cheat sheet for exams

If you need to take CSCE 222 he is by far your best bet. He is very fair in his grading. Lets you use a cheat sheet on the exams and there are always extra credit questions on the exam. In the first 2 exams it seemed liked there was always one too many questions on the exam so I didnt finish. But the final was super easy and wasnt cumulative.
